content.title: About
content.content: Dulce de leche is a sweet caramelized milk paste made by slowly heating milk with sugar until the mixture thickens and turns a golden‑brown color. It has a smooth, creamy flavor with notes of caramel and vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A traditional dessert throughout Latin America, especially in Argentina, Uruguay and Peru.
The name “dulce de leche” translates to “sweet from milk”.
In some regions it is called “cajeta” (Mexico) or “manjar blanco” (Chile).
Originally prepared in large copper cauldrons over open fire.
Many variations exist, adding vanilla, coconut, chocolate or nuts.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The milk base provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Milk protein helps maintain muscle tissue.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Heat‑processed milk retains vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: High carbohydrate content quickly replenishes glycogen stores.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Caramelization creates melanoidins that have antioxidant properties.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large servings can raise blood glucose levels and contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should limit intake or choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic individuals may react to casein and whey proteins.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One tablespoon provides about 60–70 kcal; moderation is key.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use dulce de leche as a filling for crepes, cakes, ice cream, swirl into yogurt, spread on toast, stir into coffee, or simply enjoy a spoonful as a dessert. It can be melted into sauces or batter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight jar in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 weeks. For longer keeping, freeze in small portions; thaw in the fridge before use.
